Docs/Training

Training

Prepare policy observations, train the six benchmark baselines, and preserve a reproducible experiment contract.

The shared training contract

Start with Installation and download the task-matched released demonstrations. The six benchmark methods use the Sharpa hand; the public task registry additionally supports other end effectors. Choose the environment from the official task table ↗ rather than inheriting an unrelated trainer default.

ContractRequired setting
Task identity<Task>-<Hand>-v1. Pass the exact environment ID and its registered robot. OpenCabinet uses CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 and panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base.
Control and actionspd_joint_pos: absolute joint targets in radians; 29 channels for one arm and Sharpa hand, 58 for both. Match joint ordering and the selected trainer’s action parameterization.
RewardTask environments expose sparse (the success indicator) and none; trainers default to sparse.
Datasetdata/sharpa/<environment ID>. Render policy images from the recorded simulator states before image-based training.
Camera contractFixed scene camera plus the task’s wrist camera(s). Use cabinet_fixed for pixel/ACT/DP preparation and robodex_fixed for VLA preparation; keep names, resolution and history consistent with the chosen loader.
Storage rootsRelative data paths resolve against $ROBODEX_DATA_ROOT; checkpoints and runs use $ROBODEX_STORAGE_ROOT / $ROBODEX_RUNS_ROOT. The repository is the default root.

Trainer arguments are defined in train/train_configs/ ↗. Run python train/<trainer>.py --help to inspect its exact CLI. Most trainers accept hyphenated flags; the GR00T examples retain their documented underscore spelling.

Recipe horizons are not a new evaluation protocol

The examples below preserve the released OpenCabinet training recipes, including their separate 400-, 500- and 600-step settings. A rendering limit or an in-training rollout setting does not redefine the registered benchmark horizon. For a final score, resolve the canonical task settings and use the Evaluation guide.

The six baselines

MethodEntry pointPolicy inputData preparation
PPOtrain_ppo_pixels.py ↗Two 128 × 128 cameras + proprioceptionRendered HDF5 for the BC anchor; LeRobot recordings for demo-state resets.
RLPDtrain_rlpd_pixels.py ↗Two 128 × 128 cameras + proprioceptionRendered HDF5.
ACTtrain_ACT.py ↗256 × 256 camera history at offsets 0, 2 and 4 + joint positionsRendered HDF5, then prepare_image_dataset.py.
Diffusion Policytrain_DP.py ↗Same observation contract as ACTSame image/history preparation as ACT.
GR00T N1.7train_groot.py ↗Fixed 256 × 256 rig + task instructionVLA render → LeRobot v2.1 conversion → modality configuration.
π0.5train_pi05.py ↗Fixed 256 × 256 rig + task instructionEpisode-labelled LeRobot v3.0 data, robot/controller binding and data contract.

The commands use OpenCabinet. To train another stage, replace ENV, its robot, task-specific observation dimensions and recipe limits together. Query utils.dex_tasks.resolve_dex_task(env_id).robot_uids instead of reusing the OpenCabinet robot for every task. Full guides: image and state baseline guide ↗, GR00T guide ↗, and π0.5 guide ↗.

Step 1 · Render the demonstrations

Policy-camera preparation restores every stored simulator frame and re-renders the fixed rig; it does not simulate the recorded actions forward. Released multi-view videos are useful for inspection, but the trainers below require their specified image/state export. The HDF5 contains the policy cameras and proprioception at each control step.

ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1
ROBOT=panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base

# PPO / RLPD: 128x128
python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$ENV --env-id $ENV \
  --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cuda \
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 --max-episode-steps 500 \
  --save-video --out data/pixels/${ENV}_128.h5

# ACT / DP: 256x256, then materialise the history offsets
python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$ENV --env-id $ENV \
  --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 --max-episode-steps 600 \
  --out data/pixels/${ENV}_256.h5
python train/prepare_image_dataset.py --pixels data/pixels/${ENV}_256.h5 --out data/act/$ENV

Use --limit N for a small preparation trial. Tasks whose stored frames toggle a render body’s visibility, such as CabinetPouringPickBottle-Sharpa-v1, need --sim-backend physx_cpu. --save-video writes both camera views of episode 0 side by side; inspect it before training. The image preparation script prints the --camera-names, --camera-map and --camera-history-offsets flags that match its output arrays.

Pixel demonstration renderer ↗ · Image/history dataset preparation ↗

Step 2 · Train a policy

ACT

ACT decodes a 25-step action chunk through a conditional VAE and evaluates with temporal ensembling. The released ACT runs use 12,000–20,000 updates on the 100 released episodes of each stage.

Diffusion Policy

DP generates a 16-step chunk with a temporal U-Net and 100 DDPM steps, then executes receding-horizon actions. Its released runs use 20,000 updates, batch 16.

Shared image-policy preparation and commands

These OpenCabinet commands select 20,000 updates and explicitly bind the camera history and 29-dimensional joint-position state. Keep camera order, normalization, state paths and action dimensions with each checkpoint.

CAMS="--camera-names base_camera_t0 base_camera_tm2 base_camera_tm4 task_wrist_camera_t0 task_wrist_camera_tm2 task_wrist_camera_tm4 \
  --camera-map base_camera_t0=base_camera base_camera_tm2=base_camera base_camera_tm4=base_camera task_wrist_camera_t0=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm2=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm4=task_wrist_camera \
  --camera-history-offsets base_camera_t0=0 base_camera_tm2=2 base_camera_tm4=4 task_wrist_camera_t0=0 task_wrist_camera_tm2=2 task_wrist_camera_tm4=4"
ENVFLAGS="--env-id $ENV --task-module tasks --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \
  --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 \
  --policy-state-mode paths --online-state-paths agent.qpos --expected-raw-state-dim 29 --expected-policy-state-dim 29"

python train/train_ACT.py --demo-data-path data/act/$ENV $ENVFLAGS $CAMS \
  --validation-ratio 0.1 --image-mean 0.485 0.456 0.406 --image-std 0.229 0.224 0.225 \
  --image-encoder-backbone resnet18 --image-encoder-pretrained --chunk-size 25 --prior-l1-weight 1.0 \
  --action-loss-groups 0:7 7:29 --action-loss-group-weights 2.0 1.0 \
  --batch-size 16 --num-workers 4 --steps 20000 --eval-every 1000 --save-every 1000 --num-eval-episodes 0 \
  --output-dir runs/act --exp-name ${ENV}_s1 --seed 1

python train/train_DP.py --demo-data-path data/act/$ENV $ENVFLAGS $CAMS --no-filter-success \
  --batch-size 16 --num-workers 4 --steps 20000 --eval-every 1000 --save-every 1000 --num-eval-episodes 0 \
  --check-env-before-training --output-dir runs/dp --exp-name ${ENV}_s1 --seed 1

The examples disable online evaluation during training with --num-eval-episodes 0; use the separate frozen-checkpoint evaluation afterward.

ACT and image Diffusion Policy training ↗

RLPD from pixels

RLPD mixes demonstration and online samples symmetrically. Its LayerNorm critic ensemble uses a random-subset minimum target; only the critic loss trains the visual encoder. This is the released configuration shared across the 30 stage tasks, with task-specific episode limits.

python train/train_rlpd_pixels.py \
  --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \
  --demo-data-path data/pixels/${ENV}_128.h5 \
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 \
  --reward-mode sparse --reward-bias -1 \
  --delta-action --delta-action-scale 0.2 \
  --encoder-arch d4pg --latent-dim-per-cam 64 \
  --encoder-grad-source critic_only --augmentation --augment-pad 4 \
  --max-episode-steps 600 --num-eval-steps 600 \
  --num-envs 1 --utd-ratio 1 --num-qs 5 --num-min-qs 2 --gamma 0.999 \
  --batch-size 256 --buffer-size 200000 --start-steps 5000 \
  --total-env-steps 600000 --eval-freq 20000 --save-freq 20000 \
  --num-eval-envs 1 --num-eval-episodes 20 --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 \
  --exp-name ${ENV}_rlpd_pixels --track

--delta-action enables residual joint-position control: a normalized action becomes a_t = clip(a_(t−1) + u × scale), and demonstrations are transformed into that same parameterization at load time. --reward-bias -1 changes the binary success reward into a per-step cost. A 200,000-transition replay buffer with two 128 × 128 cameras requires approximately 19 GiB of host RAM.

PPO from pixels

Online PPO uses the same visual observation, with demonstrations anchoring it twice: a BC loss on the rendered HDF5, including a pure-BC warm-up, and demonstration-state resets from the LeRobot dataset under a reverse curriculum. Its 64 collection environments require GPU physics.

python train/train_ppo_pixels.py \
  --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT \
  --control-mode pd_joint_pos --reward-mode sparse \
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 \
  --max-episode-steps 400 \
  --num-envs 64 --num-steps 200 --num-minibatches 32 --update-epochs 1 \
  --total-timesteps 5000000 --stop-at-step 1000000 \
  --learning-rate 3e-4 --actor-learning-rate 3e-5 \
  --gamma 0.99 --gae-lambda 0.95 --clip-coef 0.2 \
  --target-kl 0.2 --kl-stop-scope policy --recompute-old-logprob \
  --ent-coef 0.0 --vf-coef 0.5 --max-grad-norm 0.5 --actor-logstd-init -3.5 \
  --action-scale-source demos --action-scale-margin 0.1 \
  --hidden-dims 512 512 512 512 \
  --encoder-arch d4pg --latent-dim-per-cam 128 \
  --encoder-sharing separate_per_head --encoder-grad-source actor_and_critic \
  --augmentation --augment-pad 4 \
  --use-bc-loss --bc-data-path data/pixels/${ENV}_128.h5 \
  --bc-coef 1.0 --bc-min-coef 0.05 --bc-decay-steps 0.5 \
  --bc-batch-size 256 --bc-loss-type mse --bc-val-fraction 0.1 \
  --bc-warmup-steps 20000 --bc-warmup-batch-size 256 \
  --use-demo-init-states \
  --demo-init-data-path data/sharpa/$ENV \
  --demo-init-prob 1.0 --demo-init-min-prob 0.1 --demo-init-decay-steps 0.7 \
  --demo-init-curriculum progress \
  --demo-init-curriculum-start-frac 0.2 --demo-init-curriculum-steps 0.5 \
  --demo-init-advance-success 0.5 --demo-init-success-window 200 \
  --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 \
  --num-eval-envs 25 --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 400 \
  --eval-freq 100000 --save-freq 200000 \
  --exp-name ${ENV}_ppo_pixels --track

--stop-at-step 1000000 ends collection at one million environment steps while all schedules retain the --total-timesteps 5000000 clock. Do not change one budget flag without reviewing the dependent warm-up, regularization and curriculum schedules.

GR00T N1.7

Use the GR00T runtime

Build the dedicated runtime with bash scripts/groot/setup_env.sh, then run these commands with libs/Isaac-GR00T/.venv/bin/python as python. Dataset conversion needs FFmpeg and the libraries used by torchcodec. Accept the Hub terms for nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B before loading its gated backbone. See model runtimes and the upstream GR00T guide.

DEX_OUT holds datasets/, runs/ and evals/. The renderer assigns one of the task’s four registered instructions to each episode, with 25 episodes per phrasing. It restores the fixed 256 × 256 rig and writes controller-ordered joint vectors.

export DEX_OUT="$PWD/outputs/groot"
STEM=$(python -c "from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task as r; print(r('$ENV').short_name)")
DS=$DEX_OUT/datasets/${STEM}_rig_vla

python utils/groot_utils/replay_to_vla_dataset.py \
  --src data/sharpa/${ENV} --dst "$DS" --env_id $ENV --control_mode pd_joint_pos \
  --proprio controller_qpos --camera_size 256 --camera_profile robodex_fixed --verify_frames 6 \
  --gpu_id 0 --overwrite
python libs/Isaac-GR00T/scripts/lerobot_conversion/convert_v3_to_v2.py --root $DEX_OUT/datasets --repo-id ${STEM}_rig_vla
python utils/groot_utils/modality_configs.py --env-id $ENV --write-json "$DS"
python scripts/groot/validate_dataset.py --dataset-path "$DS" --env-id $ENV

The converter changes the dataset at $DS to LeRobot v2.1 for GR00T and preserves its original v3.0 copy at <dataset name>_v3.0. Keep that copy for π0.5. --overwrite rebuilds the selected generated dataset; choose a new output path if an existing export must be retained. Rendering and conversion details ↗

Full-parameter fine-tuning of GR00T N1.7-3B unfreezes vision and language backbones: effective batch 32, learning rate 4 × 10−5, 12,000 updates, one 80 GB GPU, approximately 64 GB used. The action-head-only option --no_tune_llm --no_tune_visual uses approximately 20 GB, but is a different training setting. Replace the local model placeholder with your downloaded nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-3B directory.

python train/train_groot.py \
  --dataset_path "$DS" --env_id $ENV --base_model_path /path/to/GR00T-N1.7-3B \
  --modality_config_path utils/groot_utils/modality_configs.py \
  --output_dir $DEX_OUT/runs/groot_${STEM}_rig --num_gpus 1 --master_port 29500 \
  --global_batch_size 2 --gradient_accumulation_steps 16 --learning_rate 4e-05 \
  --max_steps 12000 --save_steps 1000 --save_total_limit 2

Checkpoints are written every --save_steps; the final directory is checkpoint-12000. Use --resume_from_checkpoint 1 with the same output directory to restore the newest checkpoint and training state. The long-horizon guide ↗ merges each complete task’s stage datasets with utils/groot_utils/merge_family_dataset.py and trains one family checkpoint with the same budget.

Keep instruction protocols explicit

The public multi-instruction GR00T release uses per-episode registered phrasings. Its checkpoint results are not interchangeable with the manuscript’s single-instruction setting. Preserve the dataset labels and declare the evaluation instruction rule; the website leaderboard remains the manuscript baseline record.

π0.5

Prepare three task-specific inputs: the robot/controller binding from the registered environment, a data contract recording camera shapes, channel names and normalization, and a file manifest of the original π0.5 Base. Data preparation runs in the simulator environment; LoRA training runs in the separate Python 3.11 OpenPI environment described in the installation guide ↗.

# After GR00T conversion, select the preserved LeRobot v3.0 copy.
DS=$DEX_OUT/datasets/${STEM}_rig_vla_v3.0
mkdir -p prep

python -m utils.pi05_utils.binding --env-id $ENV --output prep/${ENV}-binding.json
python -m utils.pi05_utils.data --dataset-root "$DS" --binding prep/${ENV}-binding.json \
  --env-id $ENV --output prep/${ENV}-data.json
python -m utils.pi05_utils.base_manifest --base /path/to/pi05_base --output prep/pi05_base-manifest.json

/path/to/pi05-venv/bin/python train/train_pi05.py \
  --dataset-path "$DS" \
  --data-contract prep/${ENV}-data.json \
  --binding prep/${ENV}-binding.json \
  --base-model-path /path/to/pi05_base \
  --base-manifest prep/pi05_base-manifest.json \
  --output-dir runs/${ENV}-lora

This example follows GR00T preparation and explicitly selects its preserved v3.0 export. If you render directly for π0.5 without converting for GR00T, set DS to that original episode-labelled LeRobot v3.0 output instead. The Base directory contains params/ (approximately 12.4 GB) from the public gs://openpi-assets/checkpoints/pi05_base bucket; use the download recipe in Evaluation.

π0.5 settingValue
Backbone / expertgemma_2b_lora / gemma_300m_lora
Single-arm / dual-arm updates30,000 / 60,000
Global batch / action horizon32 / 30
Resume--resume restores the latest complete training checkpoint, optimizer and RNG state.

Use train/train_pi05.py for both fine-tuning and --evaluate. The current fine-tuning guide ↗ defines the exact model/runtime pins and checkpoint contract. Released inference-only overlays are not optimizer/RNG checkpoints and cannot be used as training-resume state.

Additional state-based agents

The public training guide ↗ also documents state BC, FQE/SARSA, AWR, CQL, IQL, TD3+BC, OPT, SAC, RLPD, Diffusion BC and DPPO. They read the LeRobot state dataset directly, without pixel rendering. For example:

python train/train_iql.py \
  --env_id CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 --control_mode pd_joint_pos \
  --demo_data_path data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 --success_only \
  --iql_expectile 0.7 --iql_beta 3.0 --bc_warmup_steps 20000 --actor_bc_weight 1.0 \
  --total_updates 500000 --exp_name opencabinet_iql --track

These additional agents are not extra manuscript baselines. Most trainers expose SwanLab/TensorBoard tracking controls such as --track / --no-track and write under runs/. π0.5 instead preserves its own durable metrics, run metadata and per-seed records; do not assume identical logging flags across every trainer.

Freeze, evaluate and report

  1. Keep the source revision, dataset identity, preprocessing outputs, episode split, seed and complete resolved configuration with the checkpoint.
  2. Declare a checkpoint-selection rule without using held-out evaluation scenes for tuning.
  3. Freeze the checkpoint and camera/action adapters before scoring the canonical task, native scenes or complete sequences.
  4. Record episode-level outcomes and aggregate using the benchmark score protocol, not the best training rollout.

Continue to Evaluation for released checkpoints and exact result artifacts, follow the end-to-end tutorial for a single task, or browse source and release references.
